verses.note: Isaac's wealth is presented as a gift of the LORD, not an achievement, yet it immediately brings envy and conflict. The verse neither despises prosperity nor treats it as safe; blessing in the land still has to be lived out among resentful neighbors.

Jacob's tithe begins from the conviction that everything he will have is God's gift: ‘of all that You give me’. The tenth is a return of part of what is already received, which is how the rest of Scripture frames giving (1 Chronicles 29:14).
